classes.label: Intensive Care Unit
classes.definition: A specialized department in a hospital that provides intensive treatment and monitoring for critically ill patients.
classes.evidence: The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) domain generates large volumes of patient data which can be used in medical research.

classes.label: Patient Data
classes.definition: Information collected from patients, which can be recorded manually and/or automatically.
classes.evidence: Increasing use of patient monitoring equipment in medicine is generating large repositories of patient data, which are recorded manually and/or automatically.

classes.label: Data Quality Assessment
classes.definition: The degree to which data is accurate, complete, and reliable for medical decision making.
classes.evidence: Trusting this data is important: along with being used for medical decision making, the data is often stored for offline analysis.

classes.label: Heart Rate
classes.definition: The number of heartbeats per minute, which can be an important physiological parameter in assessing patient health.
classes.evidence: a recorded heart rate of 120 may be identified as an error by a simple threshold based rule, but if the patient was suffering from sepsis at the same time, then the value may actually be a symptom of that disorder.

classes.label: Sepsis
classes.definition: A life-threatening condition caused by the body's response to an infection, which can affect heart rate among other physiological parameters.
classes.evidence: if the patient was suffering from sepsis at the same time, then the value may actually be a symptom of that disorder.

classes.label: Patient
classes.definition: An individual receiving medical care or treatment, represented in the patient data ontology.
classes.evidence: the pd:Patient as a ssn:FeatureOfInterest

classes.label: Session
classes.definition: A defined period during which patient observations and data are collected.
classes.evidence: provides classes for representing Patients, Sessions, and Timepoints

classes.label: Timepoint
classes.definition: A specific moment in time associated with a set of readings in patient data.
classes.evidence: Each Timepoint is associated with a set of Readings

classes.label: Reading
classes.definition: A recorded observation value associated with a parameter being monitored.
classes.evidence: define pd:Reading as a subclass of ssn:ObservationValue

classes.label: Parameter
classes.definition: A measurable characteristic or variable being observed in patient data.
classes.evidence: pd:Parameter (representing things that were recorded)

classes.label: Observation
classes.definition: A recorded measurement or assessment derived from patient data.
classes.evidence: pd:Timepoint as a set of observations

classes.label: Machine
classes.definition: A device used for medical evaluation, represented in the medical machine/sensor ontology.
classes.evidence: We have defined mms:Machine as a subclass of ssn:Platform

classes.label: Sensor
classes.definition: A device that detects and measures physical properties, used in medical evaluations.
classes.evidence: various subclasses of ssn:Sensor for the different types of sensors on the machine

classes.label: Sensing Process
classes.definition: The process by which a sensor collects data from a parameter.
classes.evidence: described in terms of the ssn:Sensing process that is implements

classes.label: Measurement Capability
classes.definition: The ability of a sensor to accurately measure a specific parameter.
classes.evidence: its ssn:MeasurementCapability

classes.label: Error
classes.definition: A classification indicating a potential issue with recorded data.
classes.evidence: annotated with 'Possible Error' (PoE) or a 'Probable Error' (PrE)

classes.label: Traumatic Brain Injury
classes.definition: A type of brain injury resulting from an external force, leading to a range of physical and cognitive impairments.
classes.evidence: for the Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) domain

classes.label: Hypotension
classes.definition: A medical condition characterized by abnormally low blood pressure.
classes.evidence: specific queries for hypotension and hypertension

classes.label: Hypertension
classes.definition: A medical condition characterized by abnormally high blood pressure.
classes.evidence: specific queries for hypotension and hypertension

classes.label: Noradrenaline
classes.definition: A hormone and neurotransmitter involved in the body's fight or flight response, often used in medical treatments to increase blood pressure.
classes.evidence: queries for effects of noradrenaline and adrenaline

classes.label: Adrenaline
classes.definition: A hormone released in response to stress, used in medical treatments to stimulate heart rate and increase blood pressure.
classes.evidence: queries for effects of noradrenaline and adrenaline

classes.label: Acceptable Range
classes.definition: A defined range of values within which physiological parameters are considered normal or acceptable.
classes.evidence: Acceptable If the recorded value is less than the min. acceptable value

classes.label: Sensor Accuracy
classes.definition: The degree to which a sensor's measurements reflect the true value of the parameter being measured.
classes.evidence: when sensor accuracies were considered

classes.label: Medical Disorders
classes.evidence: [inferred] Intermediate category introduced by Chain-of-Layer taxonomy construction.

classes.label: Treatments
classes.evidence: [inferred] Intermediate category introduced by Chain-of-Layer taxonomy construction.

relations.label: assesses
relations.definition: Links the quality of data to the patient data being evaluated.
relations.evidence: we argue these assessments do not consider the complexities of real world datasets and need to be extended to include context dependent assessments.

relations.label: has monitoring data
relations.definition: Links a timepoint to the set of observations recorded at that specific moment.
relations.evidence: pd:Timepoint as a set of observations

relations.label: produced by sensor
relations.definition: Indicates that a sensor generates a specific reading based on its measurements.

relations.label: receives therapy
relations.definition: Indicates that the acceptable range may be influenced by the presence of hypotension.
relations.evidence: a number of readings identified by Acceptable Range Rules 1 & 2 may have been affected by hypotension (85.6%)

relations.label: receives therapy
relations.definition: Indicates that the acceptable range may be influenced by the presence of hypertension.
relations.evidence: a number of readings identified by Acceptable Range Rules 1 & 2 may have been affected by hypertension (91%)

relations.label: receives therapy
relations.definition: Indicates that the acceptable range may be influenced by the administration of noradrenaline.
relations.evidence: a number of readings identified by Acceptable Range Rules 1 & 2 may have been affected by noradrenaline (24.2%)

relations.label: receives therapy
relations.definition: Indicates that the acceptable range may be influenced by the administration of adrenaline.
relations.evidence: a number of readings identified by Acceptable Range Rules 1 & 2 may have been affected by adrenaline (6.7%)

relations.label: has error
relations.definition: Indicates that a specific patient data entry contains an error.
relations.evidence: error rates of between 2.3% and 26.9% are common

relations.label: is affected by
relations.definition: Indicates that the heart rate can be influenced by the presence of sepsis.
relations.evidence: a recorded heart rate of 120 may be identified as an error by a simple threshold based rule, but if the patient was suffering from sepsis

relations.label: has measurement capability
relations.definition: Indicates that a sensor possesses the ability to measure a specific parameter.

relations.label: has session
relations.definition: A patient is associated with one or more sessions during which observations are made.
relations.evidence: The Patient Data (pd) ontology provides classes for representing Patients, Sessions, and Timepoints.

relations.label: has timepoint
relations.definition: A session is associated with specific timepoints that indicate when observations were made.
relations.evidence: Each Timepoint is associated with a set of Readings which refer to the Parameter being observed and its value.

relations.label: has monitoring data
relations.definition: An observation is associated with a specific parameter that it measures.
relations.evidence: pd:Reading as a subclass of ssn:ObservationValue (which represents the value produced by some sensing process)

relations.label: produced by
relations.definition: Indicates that a machine is responsible for producing a sensor's readings.
relations.evidence: we capture details of the sensors that were responsible for producing the pd:Readings.

relations.label: implements
relations.definition: Indicates that a sensor is associated with a specific sensing process.
relations.evidence: Each sensor is then described in terms of the ssn:Sensing process that is implements.
